reasons.fidelity: Every acceptance criterion of the ticket maps to AC-1 to AC-8, the receipt stays on MoneyWithdrawn v1, and every addition the ticket leaves open (currency mismatch, closed wallet, zero threshold, the one-minute target) is a D or a Q with its assumption. The one exception is 'no route reads the threshold back', which is put out of scope without being asked.
reasons.questions: The questions point at real gaps: how the email names a wallet, the time zone, a late alert, telling the customer when a threshold is removed, the missing auth and migrations, and an existing 100-row starvation bug that threatens the one-minute target. Each has an assumption and says what it blocks. Only Q-12 is close to trivial.
reasons.rules: The design keeps the tactical and transaction-script styles: invariants in Wallet, the translator in the outbox, a dedupe consumer, PER-11-safe migrations (the enum value gets its own migration), and a proper W-1 waiver with an ADR for UC-06 and SEC-02. But it files deviations from PUB-01 and MAP-01 as non-blocking questions instead of waivers, and stretches AGG-12 to cover a single optional value.
reasons.reuse: It extends what exists and describes it accurately: Money, CurrencyMismatch and WalletIsClosed, WalletMapper, WalletEventsTranslator, IntegrationConsumer with processed_message, the notification table and its index, PendingNotificationsScheduler, EmailSender and SmtpEmailSender. The facts it states about the repo are correct (no migrations folder, listPending(100), a single unit test).
reasons.coherence: Names stay the same from the glossary through the model, events, contracts, columns, tests and files, and the increments go inside out with the routes last for a stated safety reason. But I2 merges untested, the operations alert and the ≤30 s interval promised 'from I6 on' belong to no increment, and the summary's blocking list leaves out Q-4.
reasons.proportion: This is a complete story design. It is heavy for one story, though: 7 PRs, 15 questions and a 50-row rules appendix, partly because of the test-infra and baseline-migration groundwork, and I2 and I6 are very thin increments.
reasons.readability: Parts 1 and 2 use concrete Alice/W1 examples, the summary covers what, where, how and what happens on failure, and every decision has a reason a reviewer can check. But D-6 (message envelope) and D-7 (nullable columns, check constraints) are technical decisions sitting in the business-validation part.

problems: Section 14, I2: the two new use cases merge with only 'type check and lint green', and their tests wait until I7, so this increment ships untested code; put it after I3/I4 with an integration test, or merge it into I7.

Section 13 and Q-3: the operations alert for an alert still pending after 60 s, and the sending interval of 30 s or less, are promised 'from I6 on', but no increment, file (notifications.config.ts, monitoring) or test delivers them.

Section 5, 'On the rules' (Q-14, Q-15): publishing LargeWithdrawalMade v1 without a documented schema (PUB-01) and without a context-map update (MAP-01) deviates from two major rules, and the design records this as non-blocking questions instead of waivers.
Summary table: the 'Blocking questions' line leaves out Q-4 (blocks I5) and Q-3 (blocks section 13), which contradicts the Blocks column of section 5.

Part 2, D-6 and D-7: these are storage and messaging choices (envelope date, nullable balance, per-kind checks) placed in the part the business validates, in wording a business reader cannot judge; move them to part 3 or reword them as their business effect.
